title: The Turned Belt
story: A sushi belt carries plates numbered in rising order, all different. The belt has turned an unknown number of places, so the list starts somewhere in the middle: 6 8 9 2 3 5. Report the position, counting from 0, of the plate with the smallest number. The belt may not have turned at all. A long belt must be checked within the operation budget: looking at every plate is too slow.

notes: Before the turn the numbers rose from the first plate to the last.

hints: Compare a plate in the middle with the last plate. If the middle one is bigger, the smallest plate comes after it; otherwise the smallest is the middle plate or one before it.
Keep two positions, lo and hi, around the part that can still hold the smallest plate. The middle is (lo PLUS hi) FLOOR DIVIDE 2.
WHILE lo is LESS THAN hi: IF the middle plate is GREATER THAN the plate at hi, SET lo to the middle PLUS 1, ELSE SET hi to the middle. Then RETURN lo.
edgeCases: a belt turned by one place
looking at every plate is over budget
